slides.head:
Final Cut gets MotionVFX built in.
Logic gets an AI assistant.
Thousands of effects built in.
slides.body: On October 27 Apple announced a November update to Apple Creator Studio. MotionVFX, the plug-in company Apple bought in March, is now built into Final Cut Pro for Mac: thousands of templates, titles and transitions, plus rotoscoping, tracking and color grading tools.

slides.head: Logic Pro gets an assistant.
slides.body: A beta assistant built on Apple models and OpenAI helps start a song, set up a vocal track from one prompt and refine a project. Stem Splitter now separates drums. It needs macOS 27 on an Apple Intelligence Mac, U.S. English only for now.

slides.head: Circle it. Describe the change.
slides.body: Pixelmator Pro adds Generate Fill: circle an area, describe the change, and the result matches the lighting, perspective and texture around it. Final Cut Pro adds text-to-image generation inside a project and 23 new transcription languages.

slides.head: Free for subscribers in November.
slides.body: The update ships on the App Store in November at no extra cost for Creator Studio subscribers. New subscribers pay $12.99 a month or $129 a year. Keynote, Pages and Numbers get assistants and MCP support, so outside AI agents can read and edit documents.

slides.head: The plug-in tax is over.
slides.body: Templates, tracking and transitions used to be a second purchase. Now they ship inside the editor, for everyone. The edge moves from owning tools to knowing what a frame should feel like. Learn taste. The buttons are free.
